render.stationsManifestPrelude: # fmtowns (VMID 196) — Fujitsu FM TOWNS, Towns OS V2.1 L51 (TownsMENU) from the System Software CD, host-native MAME.

spa.eraLabel: 1995 · FM TOWNS — Towns OS V2.1 L51

museum.arch: Intel 80386/486-class (FM TOWNS II), 4-6 MB, Towns sprite/CD-ROM chipset
eraSoftware: MS-DOS 6.2 for FM TOWNS (kernel under Towns OS)
museum.periodBrowser: none — Towns OS V2.1 L51 ships no TCP/IP stack by default
museum.blurb: Fujitsu's 1989 CD-ROM-first home computer, a Japanese 386 whose operating system boots from the CD it shipped with. Towns OS V2.1 L51 comes up in TownsMENU, an icon desktop over MS-DOS with the CD-ROM as the boot volume — a multimedia machine years before the PC caught up.
museum.notes: Host-native station: MAME's fmtowns-family driver runs on the host (drawshm frames, ctlsock keys, FIFO audio), no QEMU and no installed guest disk — the Towns System Software V2.1 L51 CD is the boot volume (-cdrom, a CHD composed by scripts/build-guests/tiles/fmtowns.sh from the bin/cue). Towns mouse on the second pad port (-pad2 mouse). See docs/lab/FMTOWNS-WAVE.md.

reset.mouse: OPEN — Towns mouse on -pad2 (MSX-protocol mouse, genuinely relative: KEYDUMP shows MOUSE_X/MOUSE_Y axis fields, no absolute port); generic ctlsock MOVEA/CLICK1 produced no observable cursor movement (docs/lab/FMTOWNS-WAVE.md Still open #1)
reset.keyboard: PROVEN — real ctlsock KEY path through the generated fmtowns.keymap (79/146 fields matched); Ctrl+Esc opens the guest's own Task List dialog, pressed again opens a different dialog, proving live input (docs/lab/FMTOWNS-WAVE.md Proofs)
reset.fixture: PROVEN — Towns OS V2.1 L51 TownsMENU desktop booted cold from the System Software CD, golden savestate captured and restore-proven pixel-identical (docs/lab/FMTOWNS-WAVE.md Proofs)

listing.reason: Native build, real CHD, generated keymap, keyboard proof (Ctrl+Esc opens the guest's own Task List dialog) and golden-save/restore (pixel-identical, 5.2s) are all proven on the framebuffer 2026-09-13, and /os/fmtowns is dark-launched and rendering the TownsMENU desktop. Hidden for ONE reason: the pointer is unproven end-to-end. UPDATE 2026-09-13 (fmtowns-ptr stream, sandbox only, not yet deployed to this live station): the axes=0 root cause is FIXED and MEASURED (setup now reads btns=1 axes=1, via mame-ctlsock-ptr-tags.patch with a type-based Mouse-X/Y binding fix layered on top -- the module's field-name match was hardcoded to "Mouse X"/"Mouse Y" but pad2's fields are named "Mouse X 2"/"Mouse Y 2"), and relative cursor MOTION is proven precisely on the framebuffer across four distinct icon targets in one session (docs/lab/FMTOWNS-WAVE.md SS Pointer, "Pointer stream 2026-09-13"). A SECOND bug was found and fixed (the MSX mouse's BUTTONS port is IP_ACTIVE_LOW, mame-ctlsock-btn-active-low.patch inverts it) but CLICK still produces no visible guest reaction after the fix -- still open, candidates listed in the wave doc. Flip listing.state to listed and stream.pointer.transport off 'none' only once a click that opens something is proven on the framebuffer, then land both patches + the native.d/fmtowns.sh opt-in + the station.env.fixture MAME_CTL_* lines on this live station and rebuild/redeploy. See docs/lab/FMTOWNS-WAVE.md SS Pointer.
